problem_summary.summary: Return the smallest absolute difference between the values of two distinct nodes in a BST.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: the root of a BST containing at least two nodes. Return the minimum difference as an integer.

brute_force.explanation: Collect every value using a queue, sort the values, and compare each neighboring pair in sorted order.
brute_force.correctness_idea: In sorted order, the closest pair of distinct values must be adjacent: any value between a candidate pair can only make one of its adjacent gaps no larger. Comparing every adjacent gap therefore finds the global minimum.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n log n) — collecting is O(n), and sorting n values dominates.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary for the queue and collected values.

optimized.explanation: Traverse the BST in sorted inorder order with an explicit stack. Compare each visited value only with its inorder predecessor.
optimized.correctness_idea: Inorder traversal of a BST yields strictly increasing values. The minimum difference must occur between adjacent values in this sorted sequence, so updating the minimum for each predecessor-current pair examines every necessary pair.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each node is visited once and each inorder predecessor comparison is constant time.
optimized.space_complexity: O(h) auxiliary for the traversal stack, where h is tree height.

edge_cases.handling: Sorting or inorder traversal compares value neighbors regardless of their tree positions.
